neighbours.label: ' from' in physical distance or separation phrases (away from, far from, back from)
fire: Keep the grill at least ten feet away from the house.
The cabin stands far from any paved road in the hills.
Plant the tree well back from the property line.
The new runway was built miles from the nearest village.
Store the fuel cans away from heat and open flames.
Their farm lies a long way from town along a gravel lane.
Set the tent back from the edge of the cliff.
The well must be dug fifty feet from the septic tank.
quiet: Keep the grill clean and covered when it rains at the house.
The cabin received a letter from the county about the road.
Plant the tree you got from the nursery near the line.
The new runway was built with money from the state.
Store the fuel cans you bought from the hardware shop.
Their farm sells eggs from free-range hens in town.
Set the tent up using poles from the old kit.
The well water comes from a deep aquifer below the farm.

notes: Probe: 'away/far from' 0.5-0.63; ' natural' (top example) only 0.1-0.19, so the label targets spatial 'from'. Quiet uses source 'from'.
